title: Use of Pythagoras’ theorem
summary: Use the relationship between the three sides of a right triangle to calculate missing lengths and solve contextual problems.
objectives: Identify the hypotenuse and the two perpendicular sides.
Calculate a missing hypotenuse or shorter side.
Model diagonals, heights and straight-line distances with right triangles.

sections.title: The relationship in a right triangle

blocks.text: Pythagoras’ theorem applies only to a right-angled triangle. Label the side opposite the right angle c; it is the hypotenuse and is always the longest side. If the perpendicular sides are a and b, then a² + b² = c².

When both shorter sides are known, square each length, add, and take the positive square root. Lengths cannot be negative. Keep the exact square-root form during working and round only if the question requests it.

sections.title: Worked example: diagonal

prompt.text: A rectangular courtyard is 9 m by 12 m. Find its diagonal.

content.text: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.

sections.verification_note: The diagonal exceeds both side lengths and 9² + 12² = 15².

blocks.text: If the hypotenuse and one shorter side are known, subtract the known shorter-side square from the hypotenuse square. Adding would produce a result longer than the hypotenuse and cannot be correct.

sections.title: Worked example: ladder height

prompt.text: A 13 m ladder reaches a wall with its foot 5 m from the wall. Find the vertical height reached.

sections.verification_note: The answer is shorter than the 13 m ladder, and 5² + 12² = 13².

sections.title: Build the right triangle from context

blocks.text: Draw a simple sketch before substituting. Vertical and horizontal directions are perpendicular, and a rectangle’s diagonal creates two right triangles. Separate any extra cable, border or path length from the Pythagoras calculation.
Use consistent units before squaring. Squared centimetres and squared metres cannot be added, even though the final result is a length.

prompt.text: A right triangle has shorter sides 8 and 15. Enter the hypotenuse.

blocks.text: Mark the right angle, label the hypotenuse opposite it, and decide whether to add squares or subtract one square.
Check units, take the positive square root, and confirm that the hypotenuse is the longest side.
